title: A NEW NAME IN A STRANGE LAND

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, 'I am Pharaoh, but without your word no one will lift hand or foot in all Egypt.' Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-Paneah and gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife. And Joseph went throughout the land of Egypt." - Gen 41:44-45 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph is given sweeping authority — "without your word no one will lift hand or foot in all Egypt." He is also given a new Egyptian name, Zaphenath-Paneah, and an Egyptian wife, the daughter of a priest. Joseph is now fully established in the highest circles of Egypt, honoured, powerful, and settled in a foreign land far from his family and his roots.

Here was a real test that success can bring. Joseph was now immersed in a pagan culture, with a new name, a new position, and a new family among people who worshiped other gods. It would have been easy to forget where he came from, to let the honours of Egypt swallow up his identity as one of God's people. Yet, as the chapters ahead reveal, Joseph never lost his faith or his heart for his family. Prosperity did not corrupt him, as adversity had not crushed him.

This is worth pondering. Hardship tests our faith, but so does success. It is often easier to cling to God in the prison than in the palace. When we are honoured, comfortable, and surrounded by a world that does not share our faith, we can quietly drift from the God who brought us there.

Whatever "Egypt" God places you in — a new job, a new status, a new environment — hold on to who you are in Him. Do not let success rewrite your identity. Remember your God through both the pit and the palace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does success tempt me to drift from God more than hardship does?
2. Am I holding on to my identity in God amid worldly honours?
3. How can I stay faithful in the "palace" as well as the "prison"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me faithful in success as well as in hardship. Do not let honours or comfort rewrite my identity in You. Whether in the pit or the palace, help me to remember and hold on to You. Amen.
